sentences.text: Limaysaurus was a medium-sized sauropod dinosaur that likely reached a length of 15 meters and a weight of seven tonnes, according to an estimate by Gregory S. Paul in 2010.
This animal possessed very tall neural spines on its back, which were simple and straight, resembling the letter 'I' rather than being V-shaped.
Its mouth contained curved teeth, a feature that distinguishes it from the pencil-shaped teeth of Diplodocus.
The holotype specimen of Limaysaurus is 80% complete and is considered one of the most complete Cretaceous sauropods found in South America.
Gastroliths, or stones swallowed to aid digestion, have been found in Limaysaurus fossils, suggesting they used them to help grind food in their stomachs.
Fossils were discovered 15 km southwest of Villa El Chocón in Neuquén Province, Patagonia, Argentina, by Lieto Francisco Tessone in 1988.
The genus name Limaysaurus comes from the Río Limay river, and the species name tessonei honors the discoverer Lieto Tessone, following a formal naming in 2004 by Salgado, Garrido, Cocca, and Cocca.
Limaysaurus shared its habitat with Andesaurus and Giganotosaurus in an environment of plains with large, shallow lagoons where the climate was mild and humid.
The phylogenetic relationship between Limaysaurus and African sauropods supports the theory of a land bridge connecting South America and Africa 100 million years ago.
Limaysaurus is classified in the family Rebbachisauridae, belongs to the subfamily Limaysaurinae, and forms a basal clade within the Diplodocimorpha.

The geological beds containing Limaysaurus date from the Aptian-Albian interval, though the animal lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately between 99.6 and 97 million years ago in the Cenomanian, with a broader estimated time range from 113.2 to 93.9 million years ago spanning the Albian to Cenomanian.
There is a debate regarding the age of the formations containing Limaysaurus, with recent studies re-dating them from the Late Cretaceous Cenomanian to the Early Cretaceous Albian.
